headline: Medium-risk pair: shared allowlisted egress and overlapping data/workspace assumptions create leakage, conflict, and cascade risks; no direct prompt-injection bridge is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct injection is not proven. However, both agents are CLI/API-oriented and could be manually bridged through copied outputs or files; cognee’s session memory and Superset’s API surface make accidental instruction reuse plausible. Uncertainty keeps this above none, but the pathway is still unusual.
conditions: IF outputs from agent_a are manually pasted into agent_b prompts or dashboards
IF a shared file or clipboard bridge is introduced between the two agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste of raw model outputs into downstream prompts
Add a fixed instruction delimiter in any handoff template
Review handoff prompts for executable-looking text
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to all inter-agent content

B_data_leakage.rationale: cognee explicitly touches personal data, finance data, support history, and documents, while both agents have allowlisted network egress. Superset’s profile does not show touched data classes, but its API surface can still receive or expose shared workspace content. Because a shared workspace is not ruled out and one agent handles sensitive data, leakage is plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF agent_b is connected to the same workspace or database as agent_a
IF either agent uploads file contents or query results to a remote backend
mitigations: Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces
Restrict network egress to approved endpoints only
Redact personal and finance data before handoff
Audit API calls for payload contents
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can operate concurrently and both expose mutable interfaces: cognee via CLI/session memory and Superset via API. The profiles do not prove shared write targets, but they also do not rule them out. If they share a database, filesystem, or deployment namespace, conflicting writes or state drift are realistic, so uncertainty escalates to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same database, filesystem, or deployment namespace
IF no external locking or transaction coordination is configured
mitigations: Assign separate storage namespaces
Use per-agent service accounts
Add a lock around shared mutable resources
Schedule writes in non-overlapping windows
requires-engineering: implement optimistic concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: cognee produces decisions, workflows, and successful implementations, which Superset could plausibly visualize or operationalize through its API. The profiles do not show verification gates, so if Superset treats cognee output as authoritative, errors can cascade into dashboards or downstream actions. This is inferred rather than directly documented, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF Superset ingests cognee-generated decisions or workflow outputs without validation
IF downstream users act on dashboards or reports derived from those outputs
mitigations: Require human review before publishing derived metrics
Add schema validation to all handoffs
Mark cognee outputs as untrusted until checked
Compare outputs against source records
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while Superset’s profile gives no residency, retention, or certification details. That mismatch is not proven, but the absence of compliance controls on the Superset side means a shared deployment could create retention or residency gaps. Because the sensitive data class is explicit on agent_a and unknown on agent_b, medium is warranted.
conditions: IF personal data or finance data from agent_a is stored, logged, or exported by agent_b
IF the deployment requires GDPR, retention, or residency guarantees not documented for agent_b
mitigations: Minimize sensitive fields before transfer
Document retention and deletion rules for both agents
Keep regulated data out of Superset unless approved
Review logs for personal-data spillover
requires-engineering: add compliance policy enforcement
